title: runstate v0.4 launcher convention
description: Pins the launcher.* topics the spawner/reaper produces: launched (spawn-intent + liveness handle) and terminated (the manner of death; only a wait()ing parent can produce it). Applied on top of the envelope schema. As in v0.3, the envelope's request_id is REQUIRED on both records: it is the launch's correlation id, minted once per launch and stamped on that launch's launched, its terminated, and the lifecycle.started of the worker it spawns. Without it a third-party death record is unattributable -- it asserts the unknowable 'the run is dead' rather than 'my launch ended', and a late or losing launch's death forges a live episode's verdict (docs/specs/launcher-record-identity.md). v0.4 dates both records (docs/specs/observer-clock.md): `t` (the spawner/reaper's wall-clock at emission) is REQUIRED and non-null -- launched dates the launch (and the never-beaconed startup crash), terminated dates the reaped death (seq orders, t measures).

request_id.description: The launch's correlation id (see the convention description). Never null on a launcher record: a launch that cannot be named cannot be reasoned about.

Launched.description: Spawn-intent plus the worker's liveness handle. status is 'running' for the reference launchers; the domain may widen (e.g. intended/failed) via a convention-version bump. t is the spawner's wall-clock at launch -- required non-null; it dates the launch, and dates a never-beaconed startup crash (a launched+terminated with no heartbeat still carries a time; observer-clock §3).

Terminated.description: The manner of death (present-nullable + reason-coupled): every key is present; the inapplicable one is null. 'exited' carries a non-null exit_code (signal null); 'killed' carries a non-null signal (exit_code null) -- the pairing is enforced, so illegal states (exited-with-a-signal) stay unrepresentable. t is the reaper's wall-clock at the reaped death -- required non-null; the finish-time and GC-age answer for a killed/crashed run (observer-clock §3, §6).
